author: Jess Reyes
description:
Booting up Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave had me feeling nostalgic. Fire Emblem as it is now would’ve been surreal to six-year-old me, who only knew “Marth and Roy from Smash.” Back then, Fire Emblem was still a niche series in the west and many of us had no idea who they were. Little did I know, these swordsmen would just be two of many Fire Emblem heroes to join the fighting game series, and Fire Emblem games would reach mainstream popularity.

I discovered Fire Emblem in the early 2000s when I first started playing Super Smash Bros. Melee on our clunky big-screen TV in the basement. It was my favorite game to play with my cousins outside of having them watch me play single-player games like Spyro: Enter the Dragonfly and The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker. We played Melee for hours that summer of 2001, eventually unlocking Marth, the blue-haired prince from the 1990's Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light. Aft
title: Super Smash Bros. Was The Best Thing To Ever Happen To Fire Emblem

description:
Helen Chiang, the veteran Xbox staffer who got promoted in July and left the company amid mysterious circumstances just recently, has shared her side of the story--but her response doesn't close the book on this saga.

title: Former Xbox Exec Shares Her Side Of The Story After Mysterious Depature

author: S.E. Doster
description:
Season 1 of Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone arrives on November 6, and this fully integrates the new Call of Duty into battle royale. The season update replaces Black Ops 7's maps with two Modern Warfare-themed maps, overhauls Warzone's movement, introduces new game mechanics, and adds an operator-skin toggle feature. Here is everything you need to know when Season 1 of Modern Warfare 4 goes live in Warzone.

Additionally, Season 1 of Modern Warfare 4 adds a new battle pass, more multiplayer maps and modes, and plenty of new DMZ content. There are four new DLC weapons to unlock for use in MW4 and battle royale. This big update also also celebrates the launch of Warzone on the Nintendo Switch 2.<
title: CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Arrives To Warzone With New Maps, Movement, And Features

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie crushed it at the box office, banking more than $400 million globally to become the most successful entry in the series ever. When will the film be available to watch at home, though?

According to Fandango, the home video release is set for November 3. That's apparently when people can buy the movie outright or rent it digitally, with a physical edition for Blu-ray coming at some point later. It will also presumably come
title: When Is Resident Evil Coming To Home Video? It Could Be Very Soon

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Developer S-Game's action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero launched on October 29 and had a massive start across PC and PS5.

The game sold more than 4 million copies over its first 72 hours. That works out to 926 units sold per minute or about 15.4 per second over the first three days.

"Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support," the studio said in a social media post.

The 4 million figure counts copies sold across both PC and PS5--the game is not available on Xbox. The game reached a record of 833,921 peak concurrent users on Steam on November 1.

The game's developer is based in China, and
title: Phantom Blade Zero Put Up Some Massive Sales Numbers

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The start of the month is a good time to be an Xbox Game Pass subscriber, as that's when Microsoft reveals the next batch of games coming to the service. November is frontloaded with new game releases before November 19--we can't imagine why--and several of them are day-one releases. Once more games are revealed, we'll update this post.

A few games have already been revealed for November, and usually, the first wave is the biggest one for Game Pass. Kicking things off is the online horror co-op game Pit of Goblin. This has been in early access since 2024, and November 3 marks its 1.0 release.
title: Xbox Game Pass Has A Busy November Ahead With Several Day-One Launches

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Rockstar's GTA 6 finally releases on November 19, and if you're looking to play the game, you'll also need a console--and those are more expensive than ever. Here's a quick buying guide to help you understand what you need and how much the items will cost. 

A console

First, you'll need a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S console. The least expensive option for buying a new system outright is the Xbox Series S, which costs $500. Unfortunately, that's $200 more expensive than the system cost at launch in 2020--there are a number macroeconomic and AI factors that drove prices up significantly.
title: GTA 6 Buying Guide: Get Ready For Sticker Shock

author: Steve Watts
description:
Popular video games have always attracted copycats, but the barrier--and timeline--for creating them has recently and suddenly been significantly lowered. The advent of generative AI and vibe-coding has made it nearly trivial for individuals with even light coding experience to pump out a fully formed copy of a popular game, or even an upcoming one. As a result, developers can have their ideas taken out from under them, siphoning money or enthusiasm for their own original ideas. 

The problem of easy copycats came to a head recently during Steam Next Fest, the platform's discoverability event that focuses on free demos of upcoming games. The recent Next Fest was awash with AI slop and even led some developers to consider abstaining from releasing demos.

To b
title: Entire Games Are Being Ripped Off By AI, And Things Are Only Going To Get Worse

author: Callum Self
description:
Resident Evil Requiem is brilliant. I don’t need to tell you that—the critical scores across the board, feedback from both fans and newcomers, and the fact that Leon Kennedy returns are enough evidence to support my opinion. Halloween may be dead until next year, but what hasn’t died is the need to defeat hordes of infected. With the latest Resident Evil game cheaper than ever, there’s no better time to buy it. You only have one day to get it at this price, though.

What makes Resident Evil Requiem one of the best horror games and one of the best entries in the franchise is how it balances the recent first-person perspective entries with the survival horror-action hybrid of older games. As Grace Ashcroft, you’re forced to deal with e
title: Resident Evil Requiem Drops To Lowest Price, But For One Day Only

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
AI clones and vibe-coded copycat games have become a huge headache for developers recently, but it looks like an update to Anthropic's Claude Code's "rules" has been pushed out. Listed under "tengu_heron_brook," the tweak to the AI now directs it not to copy games and assets, and users cannot disable this setting.

Spotted by Chasm on X (via Game Developer), the full rule reads, "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don't build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original". Anthropic's Addy Osmani added that "two sentences" were added to Claude Code's prompt on Opus 5.5,
title: Claude Code Just Got A New Rule: Stop Copying Other People’s Games

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Doom developer id Software was among the numerous Microsoft-owned game studios that cut staff recently as part of the big Xbox "reset." What's the vibe like internally at the studio in the wake of that? Studio co-director Marty Stratton said in a recent interview, "We're doing great."

He said he wasn't trying to "handwave" the layoffs, and isn't shying away from acknowledging that "half of our studio" was laid off,
title: Doom Dev Says “We’re Doing Great” After Half The Studio Was Just Laid Off

author: Chris Compendio
description:
Fans have speculated on which studio is leading the development of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake since it was first announced, and a new Ask the Developer feature from Nintendo appears to give us the answer.

The interviewees in Nintendo's online feature include longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma and several members of Nintendo Entertainment Planning & Development (EPD) Production Group No. 3, which is the team behind the mainline Zelda games. In other words, the usual Zelda people are making the new Zelda game, as opposed to another studio like Monolith Soft or Grezzo.

Those other two studios have come up in fan discussions about the Ocarina of Time remake, due to their respective histories contributing to the Zelda franchise. Grezzo was behind
title: We Finally Know Who Made The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake

author: Kenneth Seward Jr.
description:
League of Legends Classic is coming to an end. As noted in a recent update, players will be able to queue up matches through Season 3 before Classic gets put “back in its box.” And while this news might not be surprising to some--it didn’t take long to notice that the majority of League’s playerbase either quickly decided that the modern modes were more appealing or outright ignored Classic altogether--I imagine this is a tough pill to swallow for Riot. That's especially true when one considers how much work went into resurrecting this older version of the hit MOBA.

Earlier this year, I spoke with game designer Brian Feeney, senior game designer David Turley, and senior animator Einar Langfjord about that work. According to the developers, there were internal debates about what should or shouldn’t be included in Classic from the start; as
title: What Went Wrong With League Of Legends Classic?

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
How much does a true console exclusive cost to make today? If recent reports are to be believed, Gears of War: E-Day had a production cost $500 million, but there's more to that figure than just a single game.

That's according to Windows Central writer Jez Corden, who says he spoke with multiple sources familiar with the story behind the half-billion dollars paid over several years to The Coalition while it was working on Gears of War: E-Day</
title: Gears Of War: E-Day’s Apparent $500 Million Budget May Not Tell The Full Story – Report

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Resident Evil is a huge success at the box office, recently surpassing $400 million globally. It's also received fantastic review scores. But hardcore fans of the game series took issue with the film and its direction because it did not contain any storylines or characters from the source material. Director Zach Cregger never intended to, instead opting for his own original story that is set in the world of Resident Evil. Now, Cregger has spoken more about the fallout, saying he became "frustrated at the conversation" around his movie and specifically how it "didn't have anything to do with the movie."

He said on The Town
title: Resident Evil Director Reacts To Backlash: “I Should Have Known Better”

author: Kurt Indovina
description:
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a 3D brawler where you can play as Godzilla 1990, hurl Godzilla 2000 across a city, and then watch Anguirus drop kick him through a building. It's hilarious. That alone is a compelling sales pitch to have me and many other Godzilla fans say, "Why, yes, please take my money." It's a pitch that follows through on its promise, which shouldn't come as a surprise considering it plays one-to-one like the original 2002 game.

It's fun to wail on giant monsters as the city crumbles around them, and that fun factor only increases when playing locally with three friends--especially if you're playing on Nintendo Switch 2 where you can pop off a Joy-Con, hand it to the person next to you, and laugh maniacally when you throw them into a pool of lava on Monster Island.
title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Is A Faithful, If Flawed, Remaster

author: Erick Tay
description: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is at its best when it simulates toy-like fantasies of playing with your kaiju, and at its worst when it prolongs your playtime with monotonous grinding.
title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Is A Faithful, If Flawed, Remaster – Review

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
With filming set to resume soon on Prime Video's God of War series, 55-year-old actor Dave Bautista revealed in an Instagram Story that he's packed on a beefy 20 pounds of muscle for the role of Kratos, bringing his weight to 250 pounds. While it's not the first time Bautista has bulked up for a role, he'd noticeably slimmed down in recent months, and he'd previously said he needed two months to get ready to play Kratos on TV.

While 250 pounds is an impressive weight, it's not the heaviest that Bautista has been during his career. At the peak of his WWE run, when he performed under the ring name Batista, the actor said he started at 325 pounds (as Deacon Batista) and once weighed 370 pounds. Over the years, Bautista usually hovered at around 290 pounds during his WWE runs, which is still massive
title: Dave Bautista Is Looking More Like Kratos After Packing On 20 Pounds Of Muscle

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
It's the start of a new month, which means new additions and departures on Xbox Game Pass. To kick off November, 14 games are being removed from the Game Pass library soon, including several simulators, one longrunning Dragon Ball game, and one of the greatest James Bond adventures of all time--at least until that upstart 007 First Light popped up earlier this year.

Simulator fans can say goodbye to Football Manager 26, Firefighting Simulator, Pigeon Simulator, and Police Simulator this month. Believe it or not, those games all come from different developers, as it feels like there's a simulator for every category and hobby out there. Another noteworthy departure is Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2,
title: Xbox Game Pass Is Losing 14 Games In November

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Nagoshi Studio, the studio formed by Yakuza creator Toshiro Nagoshi at NetEase, has been shut down before it even released its first game. According to Gematsu, shareholders officially dissolved the developer on October 31 via a resolution later published in the Japanese government gazette Kanpo.

Under Nagoshi, the studio worked on Gang of Dragon, a new game that looked similar to the veteran developer's work on Sega's Yakuza and Like a Dragon series at Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio. Work on the game continued over the years, and a trailer was shown at The Game Awards last year, but in March, reports said NetEase had pulled its funding for the project. The
title: Gang Of Dragon Won’t Be The First Game From Nagoshi Studio. It Won’t Be Any Game At All
